A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ORIGEN, with matching authors, research objectives, methods, and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original orientation-grounding experiments, a toy simulation, and a human preference study, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental and user-study results and adds baseline comparisons, ablation results, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes from returning the final latent to returning the highest-reward latent encountered. Equations 6 and 8 also remove the reward-gradient term from multiplication by sqrt(1−gamma). These are limited procedural revisions within the retained orientation reward, Langevin sampling, and adaptive time-rescaling framework.

E1.justification: ORIBENCH renames the existing COCO-derived coverage: single-object, multiple-object, general three-angle, and primitive-view evaluation. The general-angle and three-/four-view scenarios already appear in v1, including its appendices. The represented object classes, toy problem, and human-study task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds DPS and MPGD to the single-object comparison. It also evaluates DPS, MPGD, FreeDoM, and ReNO against ORIGEN on multiple objects and general orientations, where v1 reports only ORIGEN results. These additions substantially strengthen comparator coverage in Tables 1 and 5.

E3.justification: The reported monitor parameter k changes from 1.2 to 0.3, eta from 1 to 0.8, and multi-object gamma from 0.3 to 0.2. The principal metrics and 50-NFE guidance budget remain. Appendix I adds a runtime/memory evaluation protocol. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 extends the time-rescaling ablation to multiple objects in Table 1 and adds inference times to the convergence analysis in Table 3. Appendix I introduces comparative runtime and memory profiling. The toy experiment and general-orientation evaluation already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The user-study filtering remains 55 valid participants from 100, with the same vigilance-test procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, ablation, and computational results. ORIGEN's multi-object accuracy changes from 0.634 to 0.692 and absolute error from 34.27 to 28.4 under revised reported settings, rather than demonstrating a same-setting gain. Existing single-object scores and the 58.18% user preference result remain. Table 6 also changes retained three-view baseline errors: C3DW from 53.53 to 64.77 and Zero-1-to-3 from 68.70 to 59.03.

T1.justification: The stated discrete approximations in Equations 6 and 8 change the reward-gradient scaling, a mathematical revision beyond equivalent notation. Proposition 1, the continuous-time SDEs, and the stationary-distribution arguments in Appendices A–C otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain first zero-shot orientation grounding across multiple objects and diverse categories, Langevin-based reward guidance, adaptive acceleration, and superior grounding relative to prior methods. The benchmark naming and open-vocabulary wording do not establish a distinct new contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that performance is bounded by discriminator quality and expands the argument that reward-based fine-tuning can degrade image quality and diversity. It narrows v1's blanket statement about unavailable multi-object baselines to fine-tuned methods and suggests post-refinement as a possible application, without evaluating that application.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through Section 4.4 and Appendices F and I: guided-baseline backbones, guidance weights, ReNO regularization, GPU specifications, image resolutions, and resource measurements. These include newly disclosed settings, not necessarily changed implementations. Some detail is lost, notably v1's explicit FreeDoM configuration of five rewinds and ten inference steps.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Stein's estimation work, score implicit matching, Diff-Instruct++, and test-time alignment without reward over-optimization, while removing ImageReward and TFG citations. It modestly strengthens positioning against reward fine-tuning; the overall related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 is substantially reorganized around explicit methodological motivations. Experiments gain shared baseline and implementation sections, while primitive-view evaluation moves into Appendix G. The appendices are reorganized and the benchmark terminology changes throughout, producing a substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Table 1 combines single- and multi-object comparisons, new computational tables appear, and qualitative grids are expanded or replaced with baseline comparisons. The toy plot adds the unguided distribution, and primitive-view displays move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens multi-object validation by evaluating four guided baselines where v1 reports only ORIGEN, and supplies useful implementation and resource information. These gains outweigh the reporting drawbacks, but unexplained changes to retained baseline values in Table 6 and reversed total/per-iteration timing labels in Table 7 limit the net improvement.
